name: Dham (Traditional Thali)
instructions: 1. Prepare the Madra by slow-cooking chickpeas or kidney beans in yogurt and aromatic spices until the gravy thickens.
2. Cook the Moong dal separately with minimal spices to maintain a light, earthy profile.
3. Prepare the Khatta by balancing tamarind pulp with jaggery and spices to create a sweet and tangy side dish.
4. Fry the Urad dal-based Sepu Badi and add them to a rich spinach-based yogurt gravy.
5. Steam the rice to perfection to serve as the base for the meal.
6. Serve all components together on a plate made of dried Sal leaves (Pattal) to maintain traditional authenticity.
description: Dham is a traditional feast integral to Himachali culture, served during weddings, festivals, and special occasions. It is a community-driven culinary art form that strictly excludes onions and garlic, relying on yogurt, ghee, and traditional spices for rich, soul-warming flavors.
